CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA
ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is filed by the claimant against the Judgment and award dated 21.04.2021 passed in MVC No.1211/2018 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'the tribunal') seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claimant aged 30 years working as building painter met with accident on 14.04.2017 and suffered grievous injuries.
He filed claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.40,20,000/- along with interest.

The tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record,
awarded a sum of Rs.5,73,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

Aggrieved by the said Judgment and award the claimant has preferred the present appeal and mainly contended that,
he was aged 34 years and earning a sum of Rs.22,000/- per month as on the date of accident.
The claimant examined the Doctor.
The Doctor assessed the NC: 2025:KHC-K:7426 HC-KAR disability of the claimant at 44%, but the tribunal has taken only 12%.
The claimant has produced medical bills to a sum of Rs.4,60,376/-, but the tribunal has only awarded a sum of Rs.2,74,700/-.
Further no amounts are granted for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges and the other heads are on lower side and therefore requested for enhancement of the compensation.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides.
4.
Learned counsel for the respondent contended that, the medical bills produced by the claimants are not affixed with seal.
As per the Ex.P.10 medical bills, the tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.2,74,700/-.
The claimant has not filed any income proof.
He met with accident on 14.04.2017.
As per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.10,250/- per month.
The claimant was aged 34 years as per Ex.P.15 Adhar Card and the multiplier was taken at '16'.

As per Ex.P.5 the wound certificate the claimant sustained fracture NC: 2025:KHC-K:7426 HC-KAR of four ribs at right chest and got severe lacerated injuries to liver, lungs, chest and abdominal region, fracture of right wrist joint and cut and lacerated would at left eyebrow and forehead.
The claimant examined the Doctor - P.W.2.

He assessed the disability under Ex.P.9 in which it is stated that, the claimant sustained traumatic chest Anilkumar vs M Shivakumar And Anr on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149897235/
2 and abdominal injury, fracture of nasal bone, which is grievous in nature.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The CT scan of chest revealed both side hemopneumothorax and collapse of basal lung lobes.

As per the observations made in the investigations in the disability certificate, the claimant revealed fracture of nasal bone and laceration of liver and bilateral hemopneumothorax, old fracture of 3rd, 6th to 9th ribs on right side and sludge and stones in gall blader and finally the disability was assessed as 44% to the entire body.
Hence, 1/3rd of 44% comes to 15%.

But the tribunal has wrongly taken the disability as 12%
erroneously and it is to be rectified.

Hence, the loss of future earning capacity is as under:
Rs.10,250/- X 12 X 16 X 15% = Rs.2,95,200/-.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7426 HC-KAR 5.
The tribunal considering the medical bills, awarded a sum of Rs.2,74,700/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
The claimant was hospitalized for 14 days.

Considering the nature of injuries, age and occupation of the claimant and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- towards transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
The claimant might have not attended any other work for at least four months.
Hence, a sum of Rs.41,000/- (Rs.10,250/- X 4 months) is awarded towards loss of income during laid up period.

Hence, the total compensation is as under:
